newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone orders ex-soldiers to surrender arms.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone orders ex-soldiers to surrender arms.

text.p: The Sierra Leone government has ordered retired soldiers of all ranks to hand over their weapons days after it said it had foiled a coup attempt.

"All those in possession of arms and ammunition should return them to the nearest police station or to the military headquarters before September 16, 1996," said an official announcement broadcast on state radio late on Friday.
The government last week announced the forced retirement of 26 senior army officers and 155 non-commissioned officers.

They include former military ruler General Julius Maada Bio, who handed power to civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah last March, and Captain Valentine Strasser, who brought the army to power in a 1992 coup. Strasser and Bio are out of the country.
Four soldiers have been arrested in connection with Monday's attempt to overthrow Kabbah's government, security sources said.
